name: CAPABLe
aliases: Controlling Anal incontinence by Performing Anal exercises with Biofeedback or Loperamide
NICHD Pelvic Floor Disorders Network CAPABLe trial
question: Do loperamide, anorectal manometry-assisted biofeedback or both reduce fecal incontinence severity in women more than oral placebo or an education pamphlet?

design.blinding: Placebo-masked for loperamide; outcome assessors masked to biofeedback assignment
design.population: 300 women at eight US centers with at least monthly bothersome fecal incontinence, normal stool consistency (Bristol types 1 and 7 excluded) and negative colon cancer screening.
design.description: Multicenter, placebo-controlled 2×2 factorial randomized superiority trial
design.locator: PMC6708078 author manuscript, Methods, Results text, Figure 1

verdictNote: No primary comparison reached significance; constipation was more frequent with loperamide.
takeaway: In 300 women with fecal incontinence, loperamide did not beat oral placebo and anorectal manometry-assisted biofeedback did not beat an education pamphlet for 24-week St Mark's score change; the combination was not significantly better than either component, and constipation was more frequent with loperamide.

reports.label: 24-week randomized report
reports.citation: Jelovsek JE, Markland AD, Whitehead WE, et al. Controlling faecal incontinence in women by performing anal exercises with biofeedback or loperamide: a randomised clinical trial. *Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol.* 2019;4(9):698-710. doi:10.1016/S2468-1253(19)30193-1
reports.followUp: 24 weeks; St Mark's score available for 266/296 eligible women
reports.followUpLocator: PMC6708078 author manuscript, Results text, Table 2

results.endpoint: St Mark's score: loperamide versus placebo
results.measure: Model-estimated 24-week change in St Mark's (Vaizey) score, pooled loperamide groups (n=155) minus pooled placebo groups (n=111)
results.note: Change −6.2 (95% CI −7.4 to −5.0) with loperamide versus −4.7 (−6.2 to −3.1) with placebo; a negative difference favors loperamide. Prespecified two-sided alpha 0.025.

results.endpoint: St Mark's score: biofeedback versus education
results.measure: Model-estimated 24-week change in St Mark's (Vaizey) score, pooled biofeedback groups (n=149) minus pooled education-only groups (n=117)
results.note: Change −5.8 (95% CI −7.0 to −4.6) with biofeedback versus −5.1 (−6.6 to −3.6) with education only; a negative difference favors biofeedback. Prespecified two-sided alpha 0.025.

results.endpoint: St Mark's score: combination versus placebo plus biofeedback
results.measure: Model-estimated 24-week difference in St Mark's score change, loperamide plus biofeedback minus placebo plus biofeedback
results.locator: PMC6708078 author manuscript, Results text (Appendix p12 cited)
results.note: Prespecified comparison of the combination with each component; alpha 0.05.

results.endpoint: St Mark's score: combination versus loperamide plus education
results.measure: Model-estimated 24-week difference in St Mark's score change, loperamide plus biofeedback minus loperamide plus education
results.locator: PMC6708078 author manuscript, Results text (Appendix p12 cited)
results.note: Prespecified comparison of the combination with each component; alpha 0.05.

results.endpoint: Leaks per day: loperamide versus placebo
results.measure: Model-estimated 24-week change in total leaks per day, pooled loperamide (n=149) minus pooled placebo (n=107)
results.note: Change −1.2 (95% CI −1.5 to −0.8) with loperamide versus −1.0 (−1.5 to −0.5) with placebo. Secondary outcomes were exploratory and unadjusted for multiple comparisons.

results.endpoint: Leaks per day: biofeedback versus education
results.measure: Model-estimated 24-week change in total leaks per day, pooled biofeedback (n=143) minus pooled education only (n=113)
results.note: Change −1.0 (95% CI −1.3 to −0.6) with biofeedback versus −1.2 (−1.7 to −0.7) with education only.

harms.note: The most common grade 3 or higher adverse event; the report gives counts for the two loperamide groups.

harms.note: P=0.62. One serious event was considered possibly related to treatment (small bowel obstruction, placebo plus biofeedback group); Table 3 lists one fatal event in the placebo plus biofeedback group.

reports.label: Constipation-symptom analysis
reports.citation: Andy UU, Jelovsek JE, Carper B, et al. Impact of treatment for fecal incontinence on constipation symptoms. *Am J Obstet Gynecol.* 2020;222(6):590.e1-590.e8. doi:10.1016/j.ajog.2019.11.1256
reports.followUp: 24 weeks; PAC-SYM data at 12 or 24 weeks for 247/296 women

results.measure: Change in Patient Assessment of Constipation Symptoms global score from baseline to 24 weeks (0 to 4; negative is improvement)
results.note: Planned secondary analysis. Loperamide plus education versus placebo plus education P=0.17; placebo plus biofeedback versus placebo plus education P=0.82; combination versus loperamide plus education P=0.147; combination versus placebo plus biofeedback P=0.600. Changes were below the proposed minimal important difference of 0.6.

results.endpoint: PAC-SYM global score by FI response
results.measure: Change in PAC-SYM global score at 24 weeks, responders (at least 5-point St Mark's improvement; n=124) versus non-responders (n=119)
results.note: Responders −0.39 (95% CI −0.50 to −0.28) versus non-responders −0.15 (−0.26 to −0.03); baseline scores were similar.
results.locator: PMC7242126 author manuscript, Table 5 and abstract

results.endpoint: Responders by St Mark's minimal important difference
results.measure: Responders (at least 5-point St Mark's improvement) at 24 weeks
results.note: 137/266 (52%) responders. Higher baseline St Mark's score (adjusted OR 1.20, 95% CI 1.11 to 1.28) and overweight versus normal or underweight BMI (adjusted OR 2.15, 95% CI 1.07 to 4.34) were independently associated with response.

results.note: 174/256 (68%) responders. Loperamide plus biofeedback versus placebo plus education: adjusted OR 4.04 (95% CI 1.36 to 11.98).
